name: Named spec files fail loud
claim_class: A claim that a prompt needing specification or reference files used the right ones.
proof_obligation: Instruction-file imports and the cross-vendor AGENTS.md convention now cover most of what this rule once did, and only the fail-loud behavior still carries weight. Any prompt that needs specification or reference files opens with a section, before the task body, listing every needed file by its exact name and stating that the files live in the repository. Naming them up front lets a human confirm they are in place before work starts, and lets the agent fail loud: report a missing file as not present in the repository and stop, instead of working from a half-remembered version of it. A prompt that needs such files and skips this section is malformed. The evidence is the report itself: it either names each required file and confirms it was present, or names the missing file and shows that work stopped there.
failure_mode: A prompt needs a specification file but never names it up front, so a missing or misplaced file goes unnoticed until the agent has already produced work built on a guess about its content, or on a similarly named file that happened to be sitting nearby.
origin_incident: No single recorded event is documented for this rule. It generalizes a recurring pattern instead: a specification exists in an authoritative location but not where the agent actually reads from, so the agent either cannot find it, reads a similarly named file by chance, or goes looking somewhere off the allowlist.
